cards.text: Jesus and His disciples arrive at Bethsaida, and some people bring Him a man who is blind. They don't just ask Jesus for help, friend. They BEG Him, the way I beg my oven timer to hurry up, except this actually matters.

cards.question: Some people in Bethsaida bring a blind man to Jesus. They beg Jesus to ___ him.

cards.text: Jesus takes the blind man by the hand and walks him along Himself. This man can't see one step in front of him, and his personal escort is JESUS, while the last hand that held me used it to shove me face-first into dough.

cards.question: Jesus heals the blind man right there in Bethsaida, in the middle of the village.
Out past the village, Jesus does something to the man's eyes before placing His hands on him. What is it?

cards.text: Then Jesus checks in, like the eye doctor flipping lenses in front of your face. He asks, “Can you see anything?”

cards.question: Jesus asks the blind man, “Can you see anything?” At that moment, the man can see everything clearly.

cards.text: The man looks up. He can see PEOPLE! Well... kind of.

cards.question: The man can see people now, but not clearly yet. What does he say they look like?
The man can see a little, but everything is still blurry. What does Jesus do next?

answers.text: Places His hands on his eyes again
Sends him to wash in a pool
Tells him to go show a priest

cards.text: Once again, Jesus places His hands on the man's eyes. And the man who just watched a whole forest go out for a stroll opens his eyes.

cards.question: When the man opens his eyes this time, his sight is ___.

cards.text: Now he can see everything clearly, sharp as a fresh stamp on cookie dough. Then Jesus sends him home.

cards.question: Jesus sends the healed man home. What does Jesus tell him as he goes?

answers.text: Do not go back into the village
Go tell everyone in the village
Go show yourself to the priests

findings.problem: Too many choices depend on guessing unrevealed details. Cards 5, 7 and 9 provide no basis for reasoning out spit, incomplete sight or trees. Card 4 is also a guess because card 3 never says that Jesus led the man out of the village before asking whether He healed him in the village. That leaves only half of the stop's eight choice cards as informed guesses, rather than most of them.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
